title: Quick games
summary: A minute's play over words already met, outside the daily list, that never moves a schedule.
description: Sometimes there is a minute and no wish to start a lesson. The quick games are play over what the lessons taught: Match pairs, Flip and match, Dictation, Sound pairs and Say it. They pay a little XP and count as practising, and they leave the schedule alone, because matching from a handful of visible cards is recognition helped by elimination, not recall.

requirements.text: Match pairs, Flip and match, the dictation game and Say it draw only on words and sentences the learner has already met; Sound pairs uses the app's built-in pairs.
Match pairs uses up to 8 Polish and English pairs against the clock, and Flip and match up to 6 pairs counted in moves; each needs at least 4 words met.
The dictation game and Say it use up to 5 sentences each and need at least 3 met; Sound pairs plays 8 rounds.
A finished game pays 10 XP, up to 30 XP from games a day.
Playing a game writes no review: no word's or lesson's next check-in moves.
Game XP is listed in the day's XP under the game's own name.
The best result of Match pairs (fastest time) and of Flip and match (fewest moves) is kept and synced, so a record set on one device is the one to beat on another; the other games keep no record.
A game played after the day's game XP is used up still counts as having practised that day.
